purpose: Guide a decision memo that makes the requested choice, viable options, tradeoffs, recommendation, and follow-through explicit.

ordered_sections.title: Document control and decision owner
ordered_sections.purpose: Identify ownership, version, status, and the authority responsible for the decision.

ordered_sections.title: Purpose, scope, requested decision, and recommendation
ordered_sections.purpose: Make the decision and recommended direction clear before supporting detail.

ordered_sections.title: Customer and business context
ordered_sections.purpose: Describe the jobs and outcomes that make the decision necessary.

ordered_sections.title: Current state
ordered_sections.purpose: Explain present behavior, capabilities, boundaries, and relevant evidence.

ordered_sections.title: Problem and consequence chain
ordered_sections.purpose: Connect the job, current behavior, evidence, failure, consequence, and decision need.

ordered_sections.title: Decision invariants
ordered_sections.purpose: State the conditions that every acceptable option must preserve.

ordered_sections.title: Partner and capability boundaries
ordered_sections.purpose: Clarify party roles, responsibilities, dependencies, and failure consequences when external or shared capabilities matter.

ordered_sections.title: Data continuity and control boundaries
ordered_sections.purpose: Describe producers, consumers, identifiers, transfer, retention, quality, protection, and recovery when data continuity affects the choice.

ordered_sections.title: Options, tensions, and tradeoffs
ordered_sections.purpose: Compare viable choices against common invariants, impacts, dependencies, risks, and reversibility.

ordered_sections.title: Recommendation and success measure
ordered_sections.purpose: Name the choice, decisive reasons, accepted tradeoff, mitigation, and measure of success.

ordered_sections.title: Actions, owners, dates, and open decisions
ordered_sections.purpose: Record authorized follow-through and unresolved decisions with accountable owners.

ordered_sections.title: Supporting appendices
ordered_sections.purpose: Provide detailed evidence or analysis without displacing decision-critical reasoning.

narrative_rules: Begin with customer or business intent rather than architecture.
Name the requested decision and recommended direction near the start.
Build the problem from job to current behavior, evidence, failure, consequence, and decision.
Describe each option by its operation, preserved invariants, impacts, dependencies, risks, and reversibility.
Explain the recommendation through decisive reasons, accepted tradeoff, mitigation, and next action.
Separate fact, interpretation, recommendation, proposed commitment, and approved commitment.
Make disagreement, tensions, and tradeoffs visible.
Do not imply that options are equally strong when the evidence differentiates them.
Use prose for causality and tables for comparable option attributes or responsibility boundaries.
evidence_rules: Trace every material conclusion to an approved claim or an explicitly labeled assumption.
Give each metric a definition, population, period, unit, comparator, source, retrieval context, and caveat.
Do not convert correlation into causation or a recommendation into an approved commitment.
Use the same comparison basis across options.
State uncertainty and missing evidence when they could change the decision.
terminology_rules: Use stable names for jobs, parties, capabilities, invariants, options, data objects, and success measures.
Define each acronym at first use unless an approved audience glossary permits it.
Distinguish responsibility, dependency, ownership, approval, and execution.
Use precise boundary terms instead of broad labels that hide which party acts.
formatting_rules: Keep the decision and recommendation in the main narrative.
Use a common comparison table when multiple options share evaluation dimensions.
Use boundary or flow tables only when they improve accountability or continuity analysis.
Apply the current organization template before default narrative formatting.
hard_fail_rules: Block publication when the requested decision is missing or ambiguous.
Block publication when decision invariants are absent.
Block publication when viable options are not compared on a common basis.
Block publication when the recommendation lacks evidence or decisive reasoning.
Block publication when evidence is fabricated, untraceable, mislabeled, or missing critical context.
Block publication when body text and tables conflict or a material contradiction remains unresolved.
Block publication when a date, owner, target, agreement, or commitment is silently introduced.
Block publication when required overview context is absent without an approved exception.
Block publication when source-specific sample facts appear in a new artifact.
Block publication when language repair changes the decision or another protected meaning.
Block any full-language-conformance status unless the configured bundle, checks, exceptions, and human review are approved.
